post.summary:
Decrypt decrypts a ciphertext Encrypt or ReEncrypt produced for the profile — of any format the profile can
read: 4 and 5 (shared, derived), 3 and 6 (wrapped) — and returns the plaintext sealed to the caller's one-time
public key. Operation "decrypt".

DecryptBatch is Decrypt over a list of ciphertexts of one scope, every plaintext sealed to the one
recipient_public_key. Operation "decrypt"; transcript label "decrypt-batch".

Encrypt opens a plaintext sealed to the profile's HPKE key and returns it encrypted in cipheron's
ciphertext format, under a key of its own derived from the current data key: format 4 (shared, derived; format
5 with associated_data), format 3 (wrapped; 6 with associated_data). Operation "encrypt".

EncryptBatch is Encrypt over a list of plaintexts of one scope. Operation "encrypt"; transcript label
"encrypt-batch".

PublicKey returns the profile's identity keys, its tenancy, its signing keys (signed by the response key) and
its key-context digest. It is answered to any caller the profile lists, without auth.

ReEncrypt decrypts a stored ciphertext of the profile and encrypts the same plaintext again, under the current
master version (format 4, or 5 with to_associated_data) — or, in a wrapped profile, under
to_tenant_key (format 3, or 6) — without the plaintext ever leaving cipheron. It reads every format the profile
can read (as Decrypt). It is how a service moves its rows to new keys; reading never requires it.
Operation "reencrypt" within the profile; with to_profile (a cross-profile move) the caller's entry needs
"export" on this profile and "import" on to_profile instead, and "retenant" on this profile when the move changes
the tenant (another tenant, or between a shared and a perTenant profile) — both sides still signed under
"reencrypt".

ReEncryptBatch is ReEncrypt (within the profile) over a list of ciphertexts of one scope. Operation
"reencrypt"; transcript label "reencrypt-batch". An item with associated_data and no to_associated_data is
refused as ReEncrypt refuses it, as that item's error.

RewrapTenantKey opens a tenant key blob and returns the SAME tenant keys (same key id, same signing key, same
creation time, same fingerprint) wrapped under the current tenant-wrapping version. Operation
"provision"; its transcripts carry the label "rewrap-tenant-key", so its answers are never CreateTenantKey's.
Refused in a shared or derived profile.

RewrapTenantKeyBatch is RewrapTenantKey over a list of (tenant, blob). Operation "provision"; transcript label
"rewrap-tenant-key-batch". Each item's tenant is checked as RewrapTenantKey's (a tenant id, the profile's
tenancy); a refusal is that item's.

Sign opens data sealed to the profile's HPKE key and signs it: in a shared profile with the active signing key
over the data, in a derived profile with the active signing key over transport.TenantSignedMessage, in a
wrapped profile with the tenant key's signing key over the data. Operation "sign".

CreateTenantKey makes a new key for a tenant of a perTenant wrapped profile — a storage key and an Ed25519
signing key, from cipheron's approved random bit generator — and returns it wrapped (tenant_key) under the
current tenant-wrapping version, for the application to store. Operation "provision". cipheron
keeps nothing: each call makes another key. Refused in a shared or derived profile.

tenant.description: The tenant the key is for.

auth.description:
Required when the caller entry has request keys (operation "provision", request digest
transport.ProvisionDigest(tenant): tenant and an empty tenant key).

recipientPublicKey.description: The one-time public key every plaintext of the answer is sealed to.
The client's one-time P-256 public key (uncompressed point) the plaintext is sealed back to.

ciphertext.description: A ciphertext of the profile: format 4 or 5 (shared, derived), 3 or 6 (wrapped); 5 and 6 need associated_data.

auth.description: Required when the caller entry has request keys.

associatedData.description:
The associated data the ciphertext was made with: required for format 5 and 6, refused for 3 and 4
(CIPHERON_ASSOCIATED_DATA). When present it is the request digest's last field (transport.DecryptDigestAAD).

items.description: 1 to batch.maxItems items, at most batch.maxBytes of payload in all.

tenant.description: Every item's tenant and blob: as EncryptRequest's.

auth.description:
Over the request transcript under the label "encrypt-batch", request digest transport.BatchDigest of each
item's transport.EncryptDigestAAD.

sealedPlaintext.description: The plaintext, sealed with HPKE to the profile's key (info binds profile, "encrypt", the tenant and the requester's request key).

requestNonce.description: 16 random bytes, new for every request: the response is signed over it, and RequestAuth makes it single-use.

auth.description: Required when the caller entry has request keys.

tenant.description:
The tenant (1 to 2048 bytes of printable ASCII, 0x21 to 0x7E): required in a perTenant profile (wrapped or
derived), refused in a shared one.

tenantKey.description:
The tenant's key blob (CreateTenantKey, RewrapTenantKey): required in a perTenant wrapped profile, refused in a
shared or derived one.

associatedData.description:
Caller associated data (1 to 65536 bytes; empty: none): bound into the ciphertext's AEAD, never stored in it.
With it the ciphertext is format 5 (shared, derived) or 6 (wrapped), which records that it is required: Decrypt
refuses it without associated data (CIPHERON_ASSOCIATED_DATA) and with other associated data it does not
decrypt. When present it is the request digest's last field (transport.EncryptDigestAAD).

requestNonce.description:
16 random bytes, new for every request (transport.NonceLen): keys_signature is made over it
(transport.SigningKeysTranscript), so the answer is FRESH — a recorded older answer (an older signing-key list
or context digest) does not verify for this request. A client checks keys_signature under its own nonce and
refuses any other answer. Any other length is refused (INVALID_ARGUMENT), none included: an answer over the
empty nonce would pass for every later request without one, for the identity's life.

tenantKey.description: Wrapped profile: the blob every item was made under, and the one to make them under.

ciphertext.description:
A stored ciphertext of the profile, of any format it can read (as DecryptRequest's; 5 and 6 need
associated_data).

tenant.description: As EncryptRequest's: required in a perTenant profile (wrapped or derived), refused in a shared one.

tenantKey.description:
Wrapped profile: required — the blob of the tenant key the ciphertext was made under (its key id must be the
ciphertext's). Refused in a shared or derived profile.

toTenantKey.description:
Wrapped profile: required — the blob of the tenant key to encrypt under (the same tenant's; usually its new
key, made by CreateTenantKey). Refused in a shared or derived profile, whose result is always under the
current master version.

auth.description:
Required when the caller entry has request keys (operation "reencrypt", request digest
transport.ReEncryptDigest(ciphertext, tenant, tenant_key, to_tenant_key)).

associatedData.description: The associated data the stored ciphertext was made with (as DecryptRequest's).

toAssociatedData.description:
The associated data the new ciphertext is made with (as EncryptRequest's); empty: none. The same bytes as
associated_data: a re-encryption keeps the binding. Empty with associated_data set drops it, which is refused to
every caller (INVALID_ARGUMENT, CIPHERON_ASSOCIATED_DATA); other bytes — or some where associated_data is empty —
re-bind the value, served only to a caller entry granted decrypt on this profile and encrypt on the profile the new
ciphertext is made in (PERMISSION_DENIED otherwise). Both are decided before anything is decrypted.

toProfile.description:
Cross-profile: the profile to re-encrypt into, served by the same cipheron (empty, or the request's own profile:
within the profile). The caller's connection identity must be listed in it with operation "import" (and in
this profile with "export", and with "retenant" when the move changes the tenant), and the target's tenancy rules
apply to to_tenant and to_tenant_key. The plaintext never leaves cipheron. Import is a write grant into
to_profile: whatever its holder can export becomes to_profile's data.

toTenant.description:
Cross-profile: the tenant in to_profile (perTenant targets; empty: the request's tenant). Refused within a
profile: a ciphertext never moves to another tenant of the same profile.

toAuth.description:
Cross-profile: required when the caller's entry in to_profile has request keys — a signature by one of them over
the request transcript of to_profile (same operation, timestamp rules, nonce and digest), held to that entry's
replay cache.

tenantKey.description: The tenant's key blob (CreateTenantKeyResponse.tenant_key's layout), one the profile can open.

auth.description:
Required when the caller entry has request keys (transcript label "rewrap-tenant-key", request digest
transport.RewrapTenantKeyDigest(tenant, tenant_key)). Authorized as operation "provision".

sealedData.description: The data to sign, sealed with HPKE to the profile's key (info binds profile, "sign", the tenant and the requester's request key).

auth.description: Required when the caller entry has request keys.

tenantKey.description:
The tenant key blob (transport.ParseTenantKey), version 1: "CPT1" | 1 | key id (16) | lp(profile) | lp(tenant) |
signing public key (32) | len (1) | wrapping master version id | created (8) | salt (32) |
nonce (12) | the wrapped storage and signing keys (96) and tag (16) — 226 bytes plus the profile, the tenant and
the version id, at most 2369 (transport.MaxTenantKeyLen). The salt makes each blob's wrap key its own. The
application stores it; deleting it (and every older blob of the same key) erases the tenant's keys.

signingPublicKey.description: The tenant key's Ed25519 signing public key (32 bytes): Sign's signatures for the tenant verify under it.

fingerprint.description: The tenant key's fingerprint (transport.TenantFingerprint), which a client may pin.

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: operation "provision", request digest transport.ProvisionDigest(tenant),
response digest transport.TenantKeyResponseDigest(tenant_key, signing_public_key, fingerprint).

sealedPlaintext.description: The plaintext, sealed with HPKE to recipient_public_key (info binds profile, "decrypt" and the tenant).

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: operation "decrypt", request digest transport.DecryptDigest(
recipient_public_key, ciphertext, tenant, tenant_key) — transport.DecryptDigestAAD, with associated_data as a
last field, when it is set —, response digest of recipient_public_key, enc and sealed_plaintext.

enc.description: As EncryptRequest's, sealed for the batch's tenant.

results.description: One per item, in the items' order.

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript under "encrypt-batch": response digest transport.BatchDigest of each result's
transport.ItemResultDigest (CiphertextResponseDigest's fields) or transport.ItemErrorDigest.

v1EncryptBatchResult.description: A batch item's result: the answer's fields, or error.

ciphertext.description:
The stored ciphertext. Shared and derived profiles: format 4, "CPH1" | 4 | len (1) | master version id |
salt (32) | nonce (12) | AES-256-GCM ciphertext and tag (16); format 5, the same
layout with the byte 5, made with associated_data. Wrapped profiles: format 3, "CPH1" | 3 | tenant key id (16) |
salt (32) | nonce (12) | ciphertext and tag; format 6, the same with the byte 6 and associated_data
(transport.ParseKeyID reads them all).

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: operation "encrypt", request digest transport.EncryptDigest(enc,
sealed_plaintext, tenant, tenant_key) — transport.EncryptDigestAAD, with associated_data as a last field, when
it is set —, response digest transport.CiphertextResponseDigest(ciphertext).

v1HpkeSuite.description:
HpkeSuite names an HPKE suite by its RFC 9180 identifiers. This protocol implements one: DHKEM(P-256,
HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM (0x0010, 0x0001, 0x0002).

hpkeSuite.description: The suite of an HPKE key; unset for a response key.

signatureAlgorithm.description: The algorithm of a response key; UNSPECIFIED for an HPKE key.

v1IdentityKey.description:
IdentityKey is a key ADDED to a profile's identity after it was made (a post-quantum or hybrid key, a later
release): the fingerprint covers it (fingerprint version 2), so a pin covers it. This release adds none, and a
client uses none: it tolerates any role, suite and algorithm here.

v1IdentityKeyRole.description:
IdentityKeyRole is what an identity key added to a profile's identity is for.

 - IDENTITY_KEY_ROLE_HPKE: A key requests may be sealed to (hpke_suite names its suite).
 - IDENTITY_KEY_ROLE_RESPONSE: A key answers may be signed by (signature_algorithm names its algorithm).

v1ItemError.description:
ItemError is one batch item's failure: the gRPC code (google.rpc.Code) and, when the single operation would have
carried one, its ErrorInfo reason (CIPHERON_…); the message is for humans. It is covered by the batch's response
signature like a result.

hpkePublicKey.description:
Identity: the HPKE public key requests are sealed to (SerializePublicKey of RFC 9180: an uncompressed P-256
point, 65 bytes). Never rotates.

responsePublicKey.description:
Identity: the Ed25519 public key (32 bytes) every response_signature and keys_signature verifies under.
Never rotates.

signingKeys.description:
Every signing key version the profile has ever signed with, in canonical order (ascending key_id), exactly one
ACTIVE, any number VERIFY_ONLY or REVOKED. Shared and derived profiles: at least one. Wrapped profiles: none
(each tenant key has its own).

keysSignature.description:
Ed25519 by the response key over transport.SigningKeysTranscript: label "cipheron/v1|signed_keys", the transcript
version (1), profile, tenancy, context_digest, the request's request_nonce, then the number of signing keys and
each one (key_id, the state's number, public_key) in canonical order.

contextDigest.description:
transport.ContextDigest of the profile's key context: "sha256:" and 64 lower-case hex digits. Members of a
group sharing the profile must answer the same one; a service may pin it (expectContext).

hpkeSuite.description:
Identity: the suite of hpke_public_key. Always written; a client refuses an answer without it and seals nothing
to a key of a suite it does not implement.

responseKeyAlgorithm.description: Identity: the algorithm of response_public_key (ED25519). Always written.

additionalIdentityKeys.description:
Identity: keys added to the identity after the profile was made (none in this release). Covered by the
fingerprint (version 2).

keyStatement.description:
The profile's key statement (transport.KeyStatement): its identity, tenancy, context digest, signing keys with
their states and algorithms and the time cipheron issued it — WITHOUT a nonce, so it can be published and
verified offline against the pinned fingerprint (the identity inside is what the fingerprint covers). It
proves no freshness: a verifier bounds its age by issued_at.

keyStatementSignature.description: Ed25519 by the response key over key_statement's bytes.

v1PublicKeyResponse.description:
PublicKeyResponse is the profile's public keys.

The profile's fingerprint (transport.Fingerprint; `cipheron keygen` prints it, a client pins it) covers the
profile, tenancy, hpke_public_key and response_public_key — the identity, which never changes — and their suite
and algorithm and any additional identity key. A CLASSICAL identity (hpke_suite 0x0010/0x0001/0x0002, an
Ed25519 response key, no additional key: every profile this release makes) has fingerprint version 1; any other
has fingerprint version 2, which names the suite, the algorithms and every key (transport.Fingerprint).
signing_keys and context_digest are not in it: they are authenticated by keys_signature, which verifies under the
(pinned) response key.

ciphertext.description:
The same plaintext, encrypted again: format 4 (5 with to_associated_data) under the current master version
(shared, derived), format 3 (6) under to_tenant_key (wrapped) — of to_profile's tenancy when set.

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: operation "reencrypt", request digest transport.ReEncryptDigest (with the
extension group transport.ReEncryptDigestExt when any of fields 9 to 12 is set), response digest
transport.CiphertextResponseDigest(ciphertext).

toResponseSignature.description: Cross-profile only: the same transcript under to_profile, signed by to_profile's response key.

timestampMs.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, when the client made the request.

v1RequestAuth.description:
RequestAuth is a caller's proof that it made this request now: an Ed25519 signature by one of the caller
entry's request keys over the request transcript (transport.RequestTranscript): label
"cipheron/v1|signed_request", the transcript version (1), the profile, the operation's transcript label,
timestamp_ms, the request's request_nonce and a digest of the request's payload fields. cipheron accepts a
timestamp within its configured skew and each nonce once. The answer's response_signature is over the response
transcript (transport.ResponseTranscript, label "cipheron/v1|signed_response", with the answering cipheron's
key-context digest).

tenantKey.description:
The same tenant key wrapped under the current tenant-wrapping version: the same key id, signing
public key and creation time, in the one blob layout (CreateTenantKeyResponse.tenant_key). The old blob keeps
opening while its wrapping version is listed.

signingPublicKey.description: The tenant key's Ed25519 signing public key: unchanged.

fingerprint.description: The tenant key's fingerprint: unchanged, so a pin survives the rewrap.

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: label "rewrap-tenant-key", request digest transport.RewrapTenantKeyDigest,
response digest transport.TenantKeyResponseDigest(tenant_key, signing_public_key, fingerprint).

signature.description:
The Ed25519 signature (64 bytes). Shared profile: over the data. Derived profile: over
transport.TenantSignedMessage(profile, tenant, data). Wrapped profile: over the data, by the tenant key.

keyId.description:
The key that signed (16 bytes): a signing key's key_id (PublicKeyResponse.signing_keys) in a shared or
derived profile, the tenant key's id (the blob's) in a wrapped one.

responseSignature.description:
Over the response transcript: operation "sign", request digest transport.SignDigest(enc, sealed_data, tenant,
tenant_key), response digest transport.SignResponseDigest(signature, key_id).

v1SignatureAlgorithm.description:
SignatureAlgorithm is the algorithm of a signing key or a response key. This protocol implements Ed25519 only; a
client keeps a key of another algorithm listed and uses it for nothing (the crypto-agility extension point). A
signing key's id binds its algorithm (transport.SigningKeyIDOf), so keys_signature, which covers the id, covers
the algorithm.

 - SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM_ED25519: Ed25519 (RFC 8032, pure).

keyId.description:
transport.SigningKeyID(public_key): 16 bytes, the first half of a SHA-256 of the public key. A client checks
it; Sign's answer names the key it signed with by it.

state.description:
ACTIVE, VERIFY_ONLY or REVOKED; keys_signature covers the state's number. A client refuses an answer with any
other state.

algorithm.description:
The key's algorithm (ED25519; never UNSPECIFIED). key_id binds it: the Ed25519 id is SigningKeyID(public_key),
another algorithm's names the algorithm too (transport.SigningKeyIDOf).

v1SigningKey.description: SigningKey is one version of a profile's signing key.

v1SigningKeyState.description:
SigningKeyState is a signing key version's state.

 - SIGNING_KEY_STATE_ACTIVE: The key Sign signs with. Exactly one per profile that has signing keys.
 - SIGNING_KEY_STATE_VERIFY_ONLY: Listed so its signatures keep verifying; Sign does not use it.
 - SIGNING_KEY_STATE_REVOKED: Revoked, for good: listed (its public key stays in the list), never signs, and a client refuses every signature
under it. The keyset records it and holds no private key for it any more.

v1Tenancy.description:
Tenancy is a profile's mode, fixed for its life. It is in the fingerprint and in the key-context digest.

 - TENANCY_SHARED: One set of keys for every caller (transport.TenancyShared, "shared").
 - TENANCY_PER_TENANT_WRAPPED: A key per tenant, made by CreateTenantKey and stored by the application as a tenant key blob
(transport.TenancyPerTenantWrapped, "perTenantWrapped"). The profile has no signing key of its own.
 - TENANCY_PER_TENANT_DERIVED: Every tenant's keys derived from the profile's keys and the tenant id; nothing stored anywhere
(transport.TenancyPerTenantDerived, "perTenantDerived").
